title: SA/213/2019 of RAJENDRA PRASAD DANGWAL Vs SRIRAM DHONDIYAL

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Second Appeal No.213 of 2019
Sh. Rajendra Prasad Dangwal
and another ......Defendants/Appellants
Versus
Shri Sri Ram Dhondiyal ......Plaintiff/Respondent
Present: Mr. Vikas Bahuguna, Advocate for the appellants.
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J. (Oral)
This is defendant's second appeal under Section 100 C.P.C., wherein
he has challenged the judgments/decree dated 10.12.2010, as passed by the
court of 1st Additional Civil Judge (J.D.), Dehradun in Original Suit No.12
of 2005, Sri Ram Dhondiyal vs. R.P. Dangwal and Another, whereby the
suit of the plaintiff/respondent was decreed for removal of construction and
encroachment which was allegedly to have been made by the
defendants/appellants herein on the disputed pathway. The said judgment of
trial court rendered in O.S. No.12 of 2015 on a challenge being given in
civil appeal being Civil Appeal No.5 of 2011, R.P. Dangwal and Another
vs. Sri Ram Dhondiyal, the first appellate court of IIIrd Additional District
Judge, Dehradun too by the judgment and decree dated 05.09.2019 had
dismissed the appeal and consequently the present second appeal.
2. The plaintiff/respondent herein had instituted a suit on
07.01.2005 in relation to the property in question, which has been detailed
hereunder:-

- 2 -
"SCHEDULE OF THE PROPERTY BELONGING TO THE
PLAINTIFF
All that property situated in Khasra No.3bh, area 0.0259 Hectares
and Khasra No.3bh area 0.0510, Total area 0.0769 Hectares,
situated at Mauza Chaksha Nagar, Dehra Dun, bounded and butted
as under-North: 10 Feet wide road; side measuring 141 feets.
South: Property of Shri Barthwal in part, side measuring 91'6"; and
also land of Shri Patwal in part, side measuring 50'6" total side
measuring 142'
East: Property of others: side measuring 73'47"
West: common road in part, side measuring 28 feets; also land of
Shri Patwal in part, side measuring 41 feet, total side measuring 69
feets."
which in fact shows the property was lying in Khasra No.3 Jha
having an area of 0.0259 hectares and Khasra No.3 Jha having area of
0.0510 hectares i.e. total area of 0.0796 hectares which was in the shape of
a pathway, which constituted to be a property in dispute in the suit in
question. The illegal and unlawful encroachment was shown to have been
by the defendant on the 10 feet wide passage existing towards North of the
property, shown by figure ABCD in the plaint map. The suit which was
instituted by the plaintiff/respondent was for the reliefs as formulated in the
following nature:-
"The plaintiff prays for the following reliefs-A. That the illegal and unlawful encroachment and construction
made by the defendants over the portion of 10 feet wide road
towards North of the property of the plaintiff as shown by
the letter 'ABCD' in the Plaint Map be directed to be
removed by the defendants and in their failure to do so the
same be got removed through this learned court at the
expense of the defendants.
B. That the costs of the present suit be awarded in favour of the
plaintiff and against the defendants.
C. That any other relief or reliefs in addition to or in lieu
thereof may also be granted in favour of the plaintiff and
against the defendants."

- 3 -
3. In the plaint map as annexed therewith with the suit, the
disputed property which is the passage in question, which was shown to be
a 10 feet wide passage it was particularly described by figure ABCD.
4. In the suit thus instituted by the plaintiff/respondent on
07.01.2005 the claim of the plaintiff/respondent, was for grant of decree by
way of an permanent injunction was based upon the fact that he has
contended that he has purchased the property by virtue of a registered sale
deed dated 25.10.1999 and thereafter he got his name duly mutated in the
revenue records. The controversy basically pertains to the fact of the exact
location of the property situated on the Northern side of the property
purchased by the plaintiff/respondent which was in the shape of a 10 feet
wide passage. In accordance with the plaintiff/respondent he submitted that
he has got full right of the user of the passage and its enjoyment and he has
got a subsisting legal right of ingress and egress from the said road to his
main property existing on the Southern side of road in question. Beyond the
Northern side of the road i.e. in opposite to the property of the
plaintiff/respondent lies the property of the defendants/appellants and one
Mr. Nainwal. The cause of action as pleaded by the plaintiff/respondent in
the suit arose when the neighbourers i.e. defendants/appellants made an
effort to encroach upon said passage shown by figure ABCD, which the
plaintiff claimed to be a public passage and he was having a vested right of
user of it. He submitted that despite of various requests the
plaintiff/respondent had not budged from their act of encroachment over the
passage, the plaintiff/respondent is said to have issued notices on

- 4 -
18.12.2004 to defendant no.1 requesting him to remove the so called
encroachment from the road and the constructions made thereon as more
particularly depicted in the plaint map by figure ABCD.
5. In response to the plaint allegations, the defendants/appellants
herein had filed written statement on 19.05.2005 attempting to deny the fact
of having encroached upon the property in dispute, which was the pathway
and further contended that as far as the plaintiff/respondent cause of action
for institution of the suit was without any basis, and apart from the fact that
it was suffering from a legal defect of being a time barred claim by
institution of the suit at a much belated stage. Based on the aforesaid
pleading, the learned trial court framed the following issues on 26.07.2005:-

6. In written statement thus filed by the defendant nos.1 and
2/appellants herein jointly on 11.05.2005 it too accompanied a site plan of
the property in dispute including the disputed passage for which the suit
was filed. In the written statement the defendants/appellants, they have
taken in defence that the so called purchase made by the
plaintiff/respondent of the property in question vide sale deed dated
25.10.1999 or its mutation of their name in the revenue records was also a

- 5 -
fact which was denied by the defendants/appellants. They further denied
that as a consequence of the so called property purchased, the
plaintiff/respondent would derive any right of his ingress and egress from
the passage in question because he submits that the passage in dispute to
which on the Eastern side exists the house of Manju Dangwal, hence the
plaintiff/respondent will not have any right of its user of the said passage.
Apart from it in the written statement they have denied to have encroached
upon the said passage in any manner whatsoever, but they have submitted
that the construction, which is said to have been raised by Manju Dangwal
i.e. defendant no.2, it cannot be said to be an encroachment because it was
based upon a sanction granted by the development authority in her favour
on 16.12.2000. The defendant no.1 denied the fact of having received the
notice as claimed by the plaintiff/respondent to have been sent on
08.12.2004. In the additional plea the defendants/appellants, have come up
with the case that the property as given in the Schedule of the foot of the
plaint in fact, does not co-inside the actual property as it was existing on
the spot and it was a non-existing dimensions which has been given in the
plaint map and it relates to the property which does not have any relation
with the plaintiff/respondent and furthermore the written statement was
based on the premise that though there being a dispute pertaining to the
exact location of the property and its identification, the suit was barred by
limitation and was not legally maintainable on account of vagueness in the
pleading and also on account of mis-joinder of the parties.

- 6 -
7. One of the issues, which would be of prime consideration and
which has only been pressed by the learned counsel for the
defendants/appellants herein in the Second Appeal is issue no.6 as to
whether the suit in question filed by the plaintiff/respondent was time
barred. However the parties before both the court below in support of the
respective claim had led their oral as well as documentary evidences
including producing the sale deed dated 25.10.1999 as placed on record by
list of documents Paper 7 Ga; and sale deed as Paper No.8 Ga/1, by virtue
of which the plaintiff/respondent contends to have purchased the property
shown by figure Paper No.8 Ga, and has also shown by the map
accompanying the sale deed, which was on record as Paper No.8 Ga. The
counsel for appellant further submitted that when the act of encroachment
persisted at the behest of defendants/appellants despite request, the
plaintiff/respondent had issued a registered notices on 08.12.2004, which
was placed on record as Paper No.9C, whereby calling upon the
defendants/appellants to refrain from their act of encroaching upon the
pathway i.e. property in dispute. The defendants/appellants in support of
their averments made in the written statement had placed copy of their sale
deed on record i.e. Paper No.27-A1 and the map sanctioned in their favour
on 16.12.2000 by M.D.D.A. i.e. Paper No.28 A apart from adducing their
oral testimony as DW1 of Manju Dangwal and DW2 as Aarti Dangwal to
substantiate their case taken in the written statement. The prime concern
which requires consideration over the controversy was as far as vesting of
title of the property with parties to the suit is concerned.

- 7 -
8. Learned trial court has framed the issue nos.1 and 2 were to
the effect firstly as to who was the actual owner of the property as claimed
by the parties to the suit and secondly as to whether the 10 feet wide
pathway which was existing on the Northern side, the plaintiff/respondent
had a right to use the same and thirdly as to whether the
defendants/appellants had actually encroached upon the disputed pathway
or not.
9. Though the said finding which has been recorded on the
aforesaid issues has been recorded as against the defendants/appellants
holding thereof that the right to use the disputed pathway has also been
equally vested with the plaintiff/respondent in accordance with the terms of
the sale deed executed in his favour on 25.10.1999 and further it had
established as per finding of facts that as far as the document of title filed
by the parties to the suit in question is concerned, it apparently shows that
the pathway, which was of 10 feet in width was being jointly utilized by the
parties to the suit for their ingress and egress to their respective parcel of
property, but in any way the said finding which has been recorded by the
trial court on issue nos.1, 2 and 3 which has been concurrently affirmed in
favour of the plaintiff/respondent would amount to be a concurrent finding
of fact it was based upon the appreciation of evidence led by the parties.
10. The basic issue and the substantial question of law, which has
been framed by the defendants/appellants and as pressed herein, would be
substantial question of law no.I, which is reproduced hereunder:-

- 8 -
"A. As to whether both the courts below have erred in law
and in facts in ignoring the fact the suit of the plaintiff is
beyond the period of limitation as per Article 113 of
Limitation Act 1963?
11. The above substantial question of law is to the effect that as to
whether the suit in question as instituted by plaintiff/respondent on
07.01.2005, would be barred by limitation, as being instituted beyond the
period of limitation as provided under Article 113 of the Limitation Act.
The said plea of limitation since was also a bone of contention, before the
trial court, which has framed the issue no.6, which was with regards to as to
whether the suit itself was barred by limitation. While dealing with issue
no.6 since it was a defence which has been raised by the
defendants/appellants in order to oppose the plaint averments and the cause
of action to the suit, the trial court has recorded a finding that once, the
defendants/appellants have taken the ground of Article 113 as a defence
with regards to the suit being barred by limitation, the burden to prove the
same is casted upon the defendants/appellants in view of the provisions
contained under Section 103 of the Indian Evidence Act, because it was the
plea raised by defendants/appellants to oppose the institution of suit itself
being barred by limitation and its decision that would be
defendants/appellants who could have succeeded in his case and plea.
12. The trial court while considering the averments made in the
written statement particularly those as contained in para no.23 and 26, the
trial court has observed that the defendants/appellants rather have raised the
construction of their residence in 2001 as claimed by them and it was the

- 9 -
said year when the construction was claimed to have been completed by the
defendants/appellants. The suit has been instituted on 07.01.2005,
according to defendants/appellants that means much beyond three years of
the so called alleged construction, as pleaded by the defendants/appellants
in their written statement which is said to have been raised only in 2001. In
response to it the learned trial court has considered the controversy of
limitation from the view of the pleadings raised in para 5 of plaint, which
has been quoted hereunder to the following effect:-
"5. That sometime in the last week of April, 2002 the
defendants started encroaching upon the 10 feet wide road
in-between their property and the property of plaintiff."
13. Specific averment has been made by the plaintiff/respondent
that the encroachment over the path was made by the defendants/appellants
in last week of April 2002 and hence, the trial court has recorded a finding
that the cause of action to institute a suit for the plaintiff/respondent for the
relief claimed therein would accrue only when the act of encroachment was
actually and effectively undertaken by the defendants/appellants i.e. in last
week of April 2002. Hence, the provision of Article 113 of the Limitation
Act will not come into play to create a bar in filing the suit, as far as present
suit is concerned.
14. Giving challenge to the judgment and decree dated 10.12.2010
decreeing suit of plaintiff/respondent by way of a decree of injunction as
against the present defendants/appellants from making an encroachment
over the pathway described as disputed property by figure nos.ABCD in
plaint map. The defendants/appellants had filed a civil appeal being Civil

- 10 -
Appeal No.5 of 2011, Shri R.P. Dangwal and another vs. Sri Ram
Dhondhiyal. The learned appellate court while exercising its powers under
Order 41 Rule 31 had framed the point of determination which finds place
in para no.10 of the impugned appellate judgment which is quoted
hereunder:-

15. Since the substantial question of law as sought to be pressed
herein by the counsel for the defendants/appellants was confined in relation
to the bar of limitation which has chanced in institution of the suit, this
Court is of the view that in view of the pleadings raised by the
plaintiff/respondent in its para 5 of the plaint, pertaining to the accrual of
the cause of action for filing the suit, was actually, when the act of
encroachment was preceded by the defendants/appellants only in last week
of April 2002, that would be the actual point of determination from where
the limitation for instituting the suit in question would accrue to the
plaintiff/respondent and not from the period since when the
defendants/appellants have alleged to have completed their construction i.e.
in 2001 because even the pleadings raised of encroachment having being
made in April 2002, in para 5 of the plaint, over the 10 feet wide passage,
was fact which was not denied specifically by the defendants/appellants in

- 11 -
para 6 of the their written statement, wherein an evasive denial has been
made, because only there was denial from the act of encroachment on the
Southern side of the property of defendant Manju Dangwal, which was
pleaded in the plaint in para 5 to be w.e.f. April, 2002, it was a fact not
denied by the defendants/appellants, hence it was rightly taken by both the
courts below the accrual of cause of action to institute the suit was the act
of encroachment made by defendants/appellants in last week of April 2002,
and not the so called date/year of completion of construction by
defendants/appellants as claimed to be of 2001.
16. Even the implications of the Article 113 of Limitation Act
which has been sought to be attracted, it is to be read with the provisions
contained under Order 7 Rule 6 of the Code of Civil Procedure to give it a
logical application for a cause of action because the rule of limitation itself
would not specifically bar the institution of the suit, under the Code of Civil
Procedure. The only precaution, which has to be taken is that the
plaintiff/respondent while instituting the suit, in the plaint has had to make
an averment with regard to the issue of limitation and the reasons
constituting to it, in the plaint itself which as per the trial courts finding, the
said specific plea was taken in para 5 of the plaint as instituted by the
plaintiff/respondent, as to the date from which the date of commencement
of the act of encroachment by defendants/appellants had accrued.
17. The defendants/appellants second appeal, the challenge has
been given to the concurrent judgments rendered by both the courts below

- 12 -
decreeing the suit of the plaintiff/respondent precisely the issue on which an
appropriate adjudication which could have been made would be on the
findings which has been recorded by the courts below. Before the learned
trial court and in particularly while deciding the suit for removal of the
unauthorized construction and of demolition of the property what was
necessarily required to establish as to whether the plaintiff/respondent
enjoys the exclusive ownership of the property or whether the
defendants/appellants against whom the decree for eviction/demolition is
sought has got any right title vested over the property, in dispute which is
being alleged to have been encroached upon by the defendants/appellants.
In the case at hand both the courts below while concurrently deciding the
case in question has held particularly the findings as that the findings
recorded on issue nos.1 & 2 which related to:-
(a) Whether plaintiff/respondent is owner?
(b) Whether the plaintiff/respondent had right to use the passage?
(c) Whether the defendants/appellants had encroached upon the
passage?
18. The learned trial court while dealing with the aforesaid issues
nos.1 and 2 has recorded the finding to the effect that as per Paper No.31
Ka i.e. a document dated 06.07.1995, it is a sale deed which has been
executed by Smt. Ratan Bala in favour of Mr. Veer Singh Rana. The
original sale deed was placed on record by way of evidence, and as per the
map annexed with the said sale deed it did show the existence of 10 feet
wide passage on the Northern side of the property. The trial court further

- 13 -
observed that in accordance with Paper No.33 Ka, which is a sale deed
dated 01.07.1998 which was executed by the predecessor owner Mr. Veer
Singh Rana of a part of the property in favour of Smt. Asha Nanda, the
original sale deed which was on record once again had showed that the
property thus sold by the deed dated 01.07.1998, yet again it was showing
the existence of 10 feet wide passage which stood fortified by the map
annexed with the sale deed Paper No.33 Ka/12. The issue which would be
of prime concern is as to whether the 10 feet wide passage, which is a
disputed passage in question, the issue is as to whether the said passage of
10 feet wide whether it could be used by the seller of the property, as well
as Anita Malhotra. The reference the name of Anita Malhotra at this stage
would be relevant to be referred because she was also a purchaser of the
part of the property from Veer Singh Rana, having purchased the same by
virtue of the sale deed dated 01.07.1998. It is after including and
considering the two pieces of land sold to Asha Nanda and to Anita
Malhotra, it constitutes to be the total land, which was purchased by Veer
Singh Rana from Smt. Ratan Bala by virtue of sale deed dated 06.07.1995
as shown by Paper No.31 Ka. Hence as per the documents i.e. the
respective sale deeds, it has been consistently recorded that on the Northern
side there existed a pathway which was being commonly used. The learned
trial court after appreciating the evidence both documentary and oral has
recorded a finding of fact that in view of the statement of the
defendants/appellants' counsel the argument was that the claim of the
defendants/appellants of the disputed passage which was based upon the
sale deed dated 25.10.1999, is said to have been executed in favour of the

- 14 -
defendants/appellants, for which none of the attesting witness of the sale
deed or its valid execution of the sale deed was proved by
defendants/appellants. As per the law of evidence in order to prove the
ownership flowing from a sale deed, the attesting witness of the deed or the
original deed was required to be considered and placed on record. Even as
per the defendants/appellants' own case, it is admitted by him that the
defendants/appellants, who are the purchaser by the sale deed has not
placed and proved on record that they had exclusive right to use the 10 feet
wide passage, which was otherwise earlier enjoyed by the seller of the
plaintiff/respondent i.e. Smt. Asha Nanda and Anita Malhotra. Since they
being the seller of the plaintiff/respondent on its sale of the property to the
plaintiff/respondent it included the transfer of rights of user of the passage
too with the plaintiff/respondent exclusively. Thus the trial court rightly
held that the plaintiff/respondent had an exclusive right to use the passage
based on his purchase made by the sale deed dated 25.10.1999 and hence
had a title vested over the property i.e. the passage and consequently the
suit was decreed.
19. Even the appellate court too while framing the point of
determination yet again framed a point of determination no.1 under Order
41 Rule 31 with regards to the existence of 10 feet wide passage and with
regard to the issue as to whether the plaintiff/respondent had a right to use.
After re-appreciating the evidence as dealt with in para 11 of the appellate
courts judgment, which is quoted hereunder:-

20. The appellate court too has concurrently recorded that the flow
of title of the plaintiff/respondent from its previous owner Asha Nanda and
Anita Malhotra had perfected, it would also result into a simultaneous
transfer of right to use the disputed passage and the said question of title
has been concurrently decided in favour of the plaintiff/respondent
alongwith the right being conveyed to the plaintiff/respondent herein.
Consequently, the issue with regards to the right of the plaintiff/respondent
for the use of property has been rightly decided in its way by both the
courts below.
21. In that view of the matter, since the explanation of limitation
itself constituted to be the part of the pleadings in the suit the provisions
contained under Order 7 Rule 6 will protect the cause of action as far as the
plaintiff's institution of the suit is concerned. Order 7 Rule 6 of the C.P.C.
is quoted hereunder:-
"6. Grounds of exemption from limitation law.-
Where the suit is instituted after the expiration of the

- 16 -
period prescribed by the law of limitation, the plaint
shall show the ground upon which exemption from such
law is claimed:
[Provided that the Court may permit the plaintiff
to claim exemption from the law of limitation on any
ground not set out in the plaint, if such ground is not
inconsistent with the grounds set out in the plaint.]"
and hence the said issue, which has been only sought to be
pressed by way of substantial question no.1 (already quoted above), placed
before this Court, is not available for argument to the defendants/appellants
in view of the reasoning given in plaint and the finding which has been
recorded by both the courts below on issue no.6 with regard to the bar of
limitation. No other issue or substantial question has been pressed by the
counsel for the appellant as framed is the memo of Second Appeal. In that
view of the matter, since the second appeal is concluded by concurrent
finding of fact so far it relates to the determinations made on issue nos.1, 2
and 3, which was dealing with the status of the path and the right of its user,
I hold that the second appeal is concluded by concurrent finding of fact
which does not involve an answer to any other substantial questions as
framed by the defendant/appellant as it does not entail consideration and as
such second appeal lacks merits and the same is accordingly dismissed.
22. However, there would be no order as to cost.
 (Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
